Alex — great conversation earlier. Quick recap and asks so we can prepare a tight pricing/POC proposal: 

- Goal: 6-week POC to validate user-facing search/assist flows. Production target (if successful): 200–400M tokens/month.
- POC expected volume: 30–50M tokens/month (mostly inference, a small number of reranks).
- Latency SLO: user-facing p95 target ~300ms, p50 target <150ms. Tail latency sensitivity is higher for search paths.
- Budget: you mentioned a ballpark for production in the mid- to high-tens of thousands / month. Can you confirm a tighter range (monthly budget) you are comfortable with for production? Also confirm whether procurement needs a draft SOW / NDA for the POC.

What we’ll produce for you after you confirm volumes & budget: two concise options (1) Hosted SLO tier — optimized for strict latency with streaming + reserved frontends, quoted as SLO-driven unit price; (2) Dedicated reserved capacity — lower unit $/1M tokens at commit with predictable throughput. We’ll include recommended batch settings, kv-cache strategy, and an estimated monthly cost table at three scale points (40M, 200M, 400M).

Attached: redwood-poc-cost-model.xlsx (spreadsheet stub) — quick worksheet we’ll fill once you confirm the numbers.

Proposed next step: send a one-page POC SOW + two cost bands by Wed (Nov 18). If procurement wants draft SOW earlier, loop them in and we’ll accelerate.

Thanks — Soojin
Sales Lead, Redwood Inference

Soojin / Karthik — quick internal analysis based on Alex’s reply (numbers pulled into redwood-poc-cost-model.xlsx):

Summary of Alex’s asks: POC 35–45M, production 200–350M, budget $15k–$35k/mo, target $/1M tokens $70–120, SLO p95 ~350ms, streaming desirable, SOC2/retention required.

Option A — Hosted SLO tier (low ops for customer):
- Characteristics: SLO-driven pricing with latency guarantees, priority routing + streaming enabled, automatic KV caching and continuous batching.
- Estimated unit price bands (illustrative): $120/1M tokens (low-latency SLO), $95/1M tokens (standard SLO with small compromises on batching), $70/1M tokens (best-effort economy, higher p95 risk).
- For 200M tokens/mo: cost = $24k @ $120, $19k @ $95, $14k @ $70.
- Latency: expected p95 under standard SLO ~200–300ms with streaming enabled; best-effort band risks 350–500ms p95 on peak.
- Pros: fast time-to-value, no infra commitments, SLO-backed fallbacks. Cons: higher nominal unit price for strict SLO.

Option B — Dedicated reserved capacity (commit):
- Characteristics: Reserved GPU pool, autoscale policies, customer-owned routing options (VPC for Private), lower $/1M tokens at commit, quantization options available.
- Effective unit economics at commit: ~$55–80/1M tokens depending on commit size and model family. For 200–350M, we can get into the $60–70/1M band with a 6–12 month commit.
- Latency: more predictable tail behavior since capacity isn’t shared; p95 typically <200ms for primary flows if we size the pool correctly.
- Pros: predictable unit economics and improved tail latency; cons: longer procurement, minimum commit, and less elasticity for unpredictable bursty spikes unless we add burst capacity which we can do.

Recommendation for proposal to BrightGate:
1) Deliver a two-column quote: Hosted SLO (three unit-price bands with explicit p95 estimates) vs Dedicated commit (commit tier with expected $/1M range + optional burst pricing).
2) Include a cost-sensitivity table for 40M / 200M / 350M tokens at unit prices $70 / $95 / $120.
3) Include latency expectations p50/p95/p99 for each option (we’ll use conservative numbers and call out assumptions: model family, seq len, quantization).
4) Add an appendix: operational playbook for POC (batching, kv-cache TTLs, streaming enablement) and a short SLA draft.

I can draft the two-column quote and SOW. Soojin — want me to prepare the initial SOW + cost table for Wed? Karthik — can you confirm the recommended default batch sizes and the expected p50/p95 numbers for the mid-size model we typically propose for search?

—Marissa
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
